title: Redwood POC weekly sync - benchmark review vs baseline provider
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results (latency & throughput) comparing Redwood to baseline provider. Redwood team presented next tuning steps (batching, quantization, prefix caching) and identified network variability as major delta. Agreed next actions: share raw logs & updated spreadsheet, run end-to-end network-emulated test, try INT4 quantized profile with prefix cache enabled, extend pilot by 2 weeks to validate canary on dedicated pool.
action_items: Maya Chen | Share updated benchmark spreadsheet + raw logs (SCTP & server logs) | 2026-06-07
Liam Ortiz | Run INT4 profile with prefix caching on dedicated pool and share results | 2026-06-11
Daniel Ruiz | Provide network trace and baseline provider region details | 2026-06-08
Priya Kapoor | Confirm dataset subset for accuracy check under quantized profile | 2026-06-09
next_steps: Redwood to send updated benchmarks and raw logs
Customer to provide network traces and baseline region info
Run end-to-end latency test with network emulation in next 72h
Try INT4 + prefix cache config, validate quality on sample prompts
Extend POC by 2 weeks if performance delta narrows
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-05 09:00 PT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya, Liam (Redwood); Priya, Daniel, Sofia (Astra Health)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is our weekly POC sync — quick agenda, we wanted to run through the benchmark results we ran this week versus your baseline provider and make sure the tuning we did last night is clear.
[00:12] Priya: yup hi, thanks, we got the deck, skimmed it, but wanted the numbers explained cause the p95 looked, uh, tighter on Redwood but baseline had some spikes.
[00:22] Liam: yeah I'll start with the numbers, feel free to jump in. So these runs were on the same model checkpoint you gave us, same sequence distribution, 512 token avg context. For Redwood on our dedicated pool configuration the median latency p50 was ~88ms, p95 ~120ms for single-request end-to-end. The baseline provider numbers you saw were p50 ~160ms, p95 ~210ms. Throughput wise we measured steady-state token throughput about 160 tok/s on Redwood vs ~90 tok/s on their endpoint under the same batching sim.
[00:46] Daniel: can I interrupt — when you say end-to-end is that from the app in our VPC or from the Redwood edge? We need to make sure the network hops are same.
[00:54] Liam: good call — for these bench runs we used a Redwood hosted runner in us-west-2 to emulate client traffic — so it did add one network hop compared to running from your internal env. We noted that in the sheet, but some of the delta looks to be network variance on baseline side, they had a couple big spikes during their autoscale events.
[01:12] Priya: ok that makes sense, we suspected there was network egress on their side. The throughput numbers are pretty meaningful — 160 vs 90 is big. What about quality when you changed quantization?
[01:23] Liam: we tried INT8 and INT4 profiles. INT8 was basically within noise for quality (AGREE score change ~0.5%), INT4 showed a 1.5-2% drop on the eval set for the small prompt subset — so there is a tradeoff. But INT4 gave ~30-35% cost reduction and latency dropped another 15% in our runs.
[01:42] Sofia: 2% quality drop could be ok depending on which flows — we'll need Priya to pick critical prompts.
[01:47] Priya: yea I can pick a 50 prompt subset for fidelity checks.
[01:50] Maya: awesome. A few other tuning notes we wanted to highlight — prefix/K-V cache was turned on for the dedicated runs which helped p95 on multi-step chat flows substantially. We earlier had it mis-configured so some earlier numbers in the sheet didn't have cache. The updated sheet has both cache-on and cache-off.
[02:05] Daniel: you said K-V cash? (laughs)
[02:07] Liam: K-V cache, sorry the transcriber loves to rename it.
[02:10] Priya: ha no worries. Can you explain how prefix caching reduces token compute for our flow?
[02:15] Liam: sure — for multi-turn flows we store the KV cache for the prefix so subsequent requests don't re-compute earlier attention states. That reduces per-token compute and gives much lower tail latency, especially for long contexts. In our runs enabling the prefix cache reduced p95 by ~25% on average for the chat trace you shared.
[02:31] Maya: also batching strategy — we recommend continuous batching with a small latency SLO knob. For example, if you allow 15ms batching budget we can increase throughput by ~1.4x with <10ms added median latency.
[02:44] Priya: what's the impact on p95 when you batch like that? For us 95th is more important than median.
[02:49] Liam: when we increase batching budget to 15ms p50 goes up a little, p95 can increase ~20ms but if you combine with prefix cache p95 is still lower than baseline. The key is workload shape — busty vs smooth.
[03:01] Daniel: did you test with our burst pattern? The spike at noon yesterday showed big slowdowns on baseline.
[03:06] Liam: yes we replayed your trace, baseline had autoscale-induced stalls during rapid concurrency increase. Redwood's dedicated pool kept steady with our pre-warm and burst buffer configuration, so the stalls were much smaller.
[03:18] Sofia: can you clarify the dedicated pool size we used? I thought we asked for 4x A100 equivalence.
[03:24] Maya: we used an approximate equivalence to 4x A100 v3 nodes — the exact hardware is in the sheet (we show GPU types, batch configs, and kernel selection notes). There's some mapping fuzziness because of instance types and quant profiles.
[03:36] Priya: about kernel selection — I remember you mentioned compiler/kernels pick different algo for long sequences, did that impact numbers?
[03:42] Liam: yeah we auto-select kernels based on seq len and hardware. For 512 tokens the kernel choice was the high-throughput path. For a small batch of long sequences we switched to low-latency kernel on those calls which improved tail. The sheet has an appendix that shows kernel choice per run.
[03:56] Daniel: how confident are you that we can replicate this inside our VPC/private deployment? Network will be different, but compute should match.
[04:03] Liam: replication in VPC is something we recommend — we can run a small private runner inside your VPC for an apples-to-apples run. That will remove the edge hop variance. We also offered an on-prem package if you need air-gapped tests.
[04:14] Priya: ok let's do a VPC runner test. We'll need instructions for the runner and what ports, and then we'll send logs.
[04:19] Maya: we'll send the runner doc and a script to collect tcpdump + latency hist on client side. Expect that in the next email.
[04:25] Sofia: quick question on security/compliance — are the logs redacted? We need SOC2 stuff for the procurement team.
[04:31] Maya: yes Redwood can share redacted logs, we also have SOC2 and ISO attestation docs. We'll attach the security pack and an audit log sample.
[04:39] Priya: perfect. Back to tuning — what's the risk of hallucination increase with INT4? Did you see specific classes of errors?
[04:46] Liam: mostly subtle phrasing changes and a slight tendency to switch to shorter responses on a couple prompts. We didn't see major factual hallucinations increase, but it's dataset dependent. That's why we want you to run the 50 prompt fidelity check.
[04:58] Maya: timeline-wise we suggest: 1) run VPC runner with our script in next 72 hours, 2) Redwood runs INT4+prefix config on dedicated and posts results by EOD Thursday, 3) customer shares quality sample picks. If those look good we recommend a 2-week extension to bake in production traffic and confirm no regression.
[05:18] Priya: that timeline works for us, pending Daniel's infra windows.
[05:22] Daniel: I can spin up the runner later today, will send region and baseline provider region for you to match.
[05:26] Liam: great — one other note on cost modeling: with the batching + INT8 we saw a 20-25% unit cost reduction vs baseline; with INT4 it's 40% but with small quality risk. We'll add both lines in the updated sheet.
[05:39] Sofia: good to have both scenarios.
[05:41] Maya: any other questions?
[05:43] Priya: not yet. One ask — can you also include the raw server logs? We'll want to check any GC/pauses.
[05:49] Liam: yes raw logs and kernel-level perf counters included in the upload.
[05:53] Maya: perfect. I'll recap next steps and action items in an email after the call.
[05:58] Daniel: thanks, useful session.
[06:00] Sofia: thanks everyone.

Meeting end. References: Benchmark spreadsheet: https://redwood.share/benchmarks/ash-poc-2026-06-05 | Runner doc: https://redwood.docs/runners/vpc-quickstart | Security pack: https://redwood.docs/security/soc2-2026.pdf

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription errors present (KV -> K-V cash), speaker labels sometimes generic in automated export.
